title: Mini Product Lab

domain.name: developer-and-ops-tools
domain.summary: A rotating set of small non-web developer and operations tools (CLIs, network proxies, background workers, incident fixes) that can be shipped in two or three focused work sessions.

product.goal: Build useful small software products while practicing specification clarification, implementation judgment, failure handling, and evidence-backed revision.

architecture_baseline.summary: Local-first CLI, proxy, or small worker implementations selected per mini-project; no web application; use the simplest architecture that satisfies the accepted specification.
data_stores: in-memory state or local files when the specification requires persistence
external_integrations: local HTTP endpoints or explicitly bounded third-party APIs
architecture_baseline.deployment: local process or disposable preview; production deployment is out of scope unless explicitly authorized

base_business_rules: Every mini-project has one user-facing deliverable and explicit definition-of-done criteria.
Functional requirements and acceptance criteria define the product scope; learning criteria must not replace them.
Complexity must be justified by a requirement, constraint, or observed failure.
base_constraints: Each mini-project is scoped to two or three work sessions with a bounded daily time budget; the learner may spread those sessions over one to two calendar weeks.
Disposable experiments run locally or in an isolated temporary environment.
A passing implementation does not by itself prove that the learner understands the design.

evolution_history.summary: Initial mini-project learning program: non-web tools, one product per one-to-two-week cycle.
